title: Military Raid on Alleged Safe House in Villas de San Miguel Seizes Guns, 2,000 Rounds
excerpt: Soldiers searched a home in colonia Villas de San Miguel in west Nuevo Laredo that authorities say was allegedly used as a safe house linked to the Cártel del Noreste, seizing two firearms, about 2,000 cartridges, 58 magazines and tactical gear.
content:
Soldiers from the Fourth Military Region and the Eighth Military Zone searched a home in colonia Villas de San Miguel, in west Nuevo Laredo, that authorities say was allegedly used as a safe house linked to the Cártel del Noreste, according to a report citing Excélsior.

During the search, authorities seized two firearms, about 2,000 cartridges, 58 magazines, assorted tactical gear and a vehicle with a theft report, according to the report.

The military commands reported the seizure of the weapons and equipment but did not say whether anyone was arrested during the search, according to the report.

The same report also covered the arrest of three alleged leaders of extortion cells in Ciudad Victoria, in a separate coordinated operation involving federal security forces. Those three men were identified only by first name and initial, and authorities said their alleged extortion schemes targeted electric utility customers and small businesses, according to the report.

Source: El Despertar, November 16, 2026, citing Excélsior as the original report.

Update — November 16, 2026: In a separate development from the same colonia, construction worker Raúl Segovia, 26, filed a formal complaint with the federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) in Nuevo Laredo, alleging that soldiers entered his home in Villas de San Miguel without a search warrant on the night of Wednesday, Nov. 11, and took his voter ID, laser visa, other identification, bank cards, cell phone accessories and 100 pesos in cash, according to Central de Noticias Tamaulipas. The complaint was registered as investigation file FED/TAMP/NVO.LAR/0001961/2026. As of the report, the military had not issued a public statement on the complaint, and the federal prosecutor’s office was continuing its proceedings, according to the report.

Update source: Central de Noticias Tamaulipas, November 16, 2026.
